title: Problems on Trains
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Problems on Trains. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

coverage: Kilometres per hour to metres per second

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Distance needed to clear an object

To pass a stationary pole, a train covers its own length. To pass a platform or bridge, it covers train length plus platform length. Two trains crossing completely cover the sum of their lengths.

Relative speed

For opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of speeds; for the same direction, it is the absolute difference. Divide the required crossing distance by relative speed. Convert speeds to metres per second when lengths are in metres: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s. A moving person is treated as another moving object.

Worked example: A 150 m train at 72 km/h passes a 250 m platform. Speed is (\(72 × 5/18=20\)) m/s; distance is 400 m; time is (\(400/20=20\)) seconds.

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Draw the train and mark how far its front travels before its rear clears the object.
  • Use sum for opposite directions and difference for the same direction.
  • Convert every speed to a common unit before division.
  • For a pole or signal, do not add a platform length.
  • Check that the result is a time.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• Pole: time = train length / relative speed.
  • Platform: time = (\(train length + platform length\)) / train speed.
  • Two trains: crossing distance = sum of lengths; use relative speed.
  • km/h to m/s: multiply by 5/18. m/s to km/h: multiply by 18/5.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    A 150 m train moves at 72 km/h. How long does it take to pass a 250 m platform?

    1. (\(15\text{ s}\))
    2. (\(18\text{ s}\))
    3. (\(20\text{ s}\))
    4. (\(25\text{ s}\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(20\text{ s}\))

    Speed (\(=72\cdot5/18=20\)) m/s. Distance (\(=150+250=400\)) m. Time (\(=400/20=20\)) s.

  2. Core:

    Two trains of lengths 120 m and 180 m move in opposite directions at 36 km/h and 54 km/h. How long do they take to cross?

    1. (\(10\text{ s}\))
    2. (\(12\text{ s}\))
    3. (\(15\text{ s}\))
    4. (\(20\text{ s}\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(12\text{ s}\))

    Relative speed (\(=90\text{ km/h}=25\text{ m/s}\)). Total length (\(=300\)) m, so time (\(=300/25=12\)) s.

  3. Foundation:

    A 120 m train travels at 54 km/h. How long does it take to pass a pole?

    1. (\(6 s\))
    2. (\(8 s\))
    3. (\(10 s\))
    4. (\(12 s\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(8 s\))

    Speed is (\(54 × 5/18=15\)) m/s. Time is (\(120/15=8\)) seconds.

  4. Standard:

    Two trains 120 m and 180 m long travel in opposite directions at 36 km/h and 54 km/h. How long do they take to cross?

    1. (\(10 s\))
    2. (\(12 s\))
    3. (\(15 s\))
    4. (\(20 s\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(12 s\))

    Total length is 300 m. Relative speed is (\(90 km/h=25 m/s\)). Time is (\(300/25=12\)) seconds.

  5. Challenge:

    A 200 m train at 72 km/h overtakes a 100 m train at 54 km/h in the same direction. How long does the faster train take to pass it?

    1. (\(30 s\))
    2. (\(45 s\))
    3. (\(60 s\))
    4. (\(90 s\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(60 s\))

    Distance is 300 m. Relative speed is (\(18 km/h=5 m/s\)). Time is (\(300/5=60\)) seconds.
